response.title: The story of Sebastia
response.summary: Sebastia is one of the most important archaeological and historical sites in Palestine.
response.narrative:
Sebastia is one of the most important archaeological and historical sites in Palestine. It is bordered by Nablus to the south-east, Jenin to the north, and the villages of Zawata, al-Naqura and Burqa.

Things to look for:
- The Roman colonnaded street - the best-known monument at the site; a long street flanked by two rows of massive stone columns that carried porticoes used by merchants and passers-by. It was the city's commercial and administrative centre.
- The Roman theatre - on the eastern side of the city, built in the Roman period for performances, celebrations and public assemblies; semi-circular with stone seating.
- The Temple of Augustus - built by Herod the Great in honour of Augustus; one of the largest temples in the region, now surviving only as foundations and some columns.

A few facts:
- About 12 km north-west of Nablus.
- Situated on a hill roughly 440 m above sea level.
- Was the capital of the northern Kingdom of Israel in the 9th century BCE.
uncertainty_notes: Gaps the AI must not fill: exact dimensions of the colonnaded street, the seating capacity of the theatre, current population figures, and the precise dating of individual tombs are not established in the source. If a request needs them, the AI must return an uncertainty note instead of guessing.
Periods describing sieges, destruction or war were left out of the child-friendly version; they are present in the reviewed source.
